The short answer

Two desktop apps coexist: "ChatGPT" (unified) and "ChatGPT Classic" (legacy chat-only). ChatGPT Classic receives ongoing model updates and security patches with no published sunset date.

If you updated the Windows desktop app and found yourself inside a Codex workspace instead of the familiar chat window, you are not alone. As of October 2026, OpenAI ships two separate desktop apps: the new unified ChatGPT app (which bundles Chat, Work, and Codex) and ChatGPT Classic (the previous standalone chat app).

Both can stay installed at the same time, and Classic continues to receive model updates and security fixes.

Quick Verdict
  • Best for: Users who want the new Work canvas and Codex coding tools in one window
  • Not ideal for: Anyone who only wants the classic chat interface without extra tabs
  • Free plan: Both apps respect your existing ChatGPT account tier (Free, Plus, Pro, Team, Enterprise)
  • Main limitation: The new app opens to Codex by default for existing Codex users; Chat is one click deeper
  • Last checked: October 2026

What Changed in the Desktop App Migration

OpenAI replaced the original ChatGPT desktop app with a unified client that merges three experiences: Chat (the conversational interface), Work (a canvas for documents and projects), and Codex (the coding agent). The rollout began on macOS and Windows in late September 2026.

If you already had the Codex app installed, updating it converts it into the new unified app. If you had the original ChatGPT desktop app, a prompt appears inviting you to download the new version. The old version is not removed automatically; it is renamed to ChatGPT Classic and remains on your system.

According to the OpenAI Help Center article updated 16 days ago, no migration is required at launch. You can keep using ChatGPT Classic indefinitely. It will still receive model updates, bug fixes, and security patches. The new app installs side by side, so you end up with two entries in your Start menu or Applications folder: "ChatGPT" (the unified app) and "ChatGPT Classic" (the legacy chat-only app).

ChatGPT vs ChatGPT Classic: Core Differences

The new ChatGPT app is a multi-mode workspace. Its left-hand selector lets you switch between Chat, Work, and Codex. ChatGPT Classic is a single-mode app: it opens directly to the conversation list and has no Work or Codex tabs.

Both apps sign in with the same ChatGPT account, so your subscription tier, custom instructions, and memory settings apply in either one. Chat history syncs across both because it lives on the server, not locally.

A key practical difference is the default landing view. The community forum post from July 11, 2026 notes that the Microsoft Store version of the new "ChatGPT" app installs the OpenAI.Codex package and launches straight into the Codex experience. Users who expect the chat window often cannot find it at first.

In ChatGPT Classic, the chat list is the only view. If your workflow is purely conversational, Classic removes the extra navigation step.

Where Codex Fits In

Codex is OpenAI's coding agent that can read, write, and run code in a sandboxed environment. In the new unified app, it appears as a dedicated tab alongside Chat and Work. If you never used Codex before, the new app still installs the Codex runtime, but the Chat tab is the default.

Existing Codex users see Codex first because the updated app preserves their last-used mode. You can change the default launch mode in Settings → General → Default view.

ChatGPT Classic does not include Codex. If you want the coding agent, you must use the new unified app or the web version at chatgpt.com. The web version also surfaces Codex under the same account, so you are not locked to the desktop client for coding tasks.

First-Time User Blockers: Cause and Fix

  • Cause: App opens to Codex instead of Chat — The new app remembers the last used mode; Codex users land in the coding agent. Fix: Click the Chat icon in the left sidebar or press Ctrl+1 (Windows) / Cmd+1 (Mac) to jump to Chat.
  • Cause: Two "ChatGPT" entries in Start menu — The update leaves Classic installed alongside the new app. Fix: Pin the one you prefer; uninstall Classic only if you no longer want the single-mode experience.
  • Cause: Missing Work or Codex tabs in Classic — Classic is chat-only by design. Fix: Switch to the new unified app for those features; your history and settings carry over automatically.
  • Cause: Microsoft Store listing shows "ChatGPT" but installs Codex package — The store entry name matches the new unified app, not Classic. Fix: Expect the unified app from the Store; download Classic only from the OpenAI help page if you specifically want the legacy client.
  • Cause: Keyboard shortcuts differ between apps — Classic has no mode-switch shortcuts because it only runs Chat. Fix: In the new app, use Ctrl+1/2/3 (Windows) or Cmd+1/2/3 (Mac) for Chat, Work, Codex; stay in Classic if you never switch modes.
  • Cause: New chat button hidden in collapsed sidebar — In the new app, the conversation list collapses when the window is narrow, hiding the New chat button. Fix: Widen the window until the sidebar expands, or click the hamburger menu (☰) to reveal the conversation list and the New chat button.
Watch out

Uninstalling ChatGPT Classic removes the chat-only shortcut but does not delete your conversations — those stay in your ChatGPT account. Reinstalling Classic later is possible from the OpenAI help center download link.

What Stays the Same and What Is Still Unconfirmed

Your subscription tier, API usage limits, and data controls are identical across both desktop apps and the web. The model selector (GPT-4o, o1-preview, etc.) behaves the same way. Custom instructions, memory, and shared links work interchangeably. OpenAI has not published a sunset date for ChatGPT Classic; the help center states it "continues to receive model updates, bug fixes, security updates" with no end timeline.

Unconfirmed areas include whether future features like advanced voice mode or screen-sharing will land in Classic, and whether the unified app will eventually become the only supported desktop client. The help center wording "no migration is required at launch" implies a future migration may be encouraged. Check the OpenAI Help Center article "Moving to the new ChatGPT desktop app" for the latest stance.

Choose by Workflow: Three Reader Profiles

Use the new unified ChatGPT app if

  • You want Work canvas for documents and projects
  • You use Codex for coding tasks
  • You prefer a single window for chat, writing, and code

Stick with ChatGPT Classic if

  • You only need the conversational chat interface
  • You want the app to open directly to your conversation list
  • You dislike extra sidebar navigation

Consider the web version at chatgpt.com if

  • You switch between devices and don't want to install apps everywhere
  • Your IT policy blocks Microsoft Store installs (the unified app uses the OpenAI.Codex package)
  • You want Codex without the desktop footprint — the web version includes it under the same account

Skip the new unified app if

  • You only need chat and never use Work canvas or Codex
  • You want the app to open instantly to your conversation list
  • You prefer a minimal interface without a sidebar

Managing Both Apps Day to Day

If you keep both apps installed, you can assign each a distinct role. For example, pin ChatGPT Classic to the taskbar for quick chat access, and use the new unified app only when you need Work canvas or Codex. Both apps share the same account, so you won't lose context when switching.

The new app's settings let you set Chat as the startup mode, eliminating the extra click to reach conversations.

Updates arrive independently: the Microsoft Store handles the unified app, while Classic updates via its own mechanism (check the OpenAI help center for the latest installer). If your IT department manages software, note that the unified app installs as a Microsoft Store package; Classic uses the older installer.

You can run both simultaneously without conflict, but only one can hold the system-wide shortcut for the Ctrl+Alt+Space hotkey (if enabled). Assign the hotkey to the app you use most.

Does ChatGPT Classic get the same model updates as the new app?

Yes. The OpenAI Help Center confirms ChatGPT Classic continues to receive model updates, bug fixes, and security patches alongside the new unified app.

Can I use Codex in ChatGPT Classic if I have a Plus subscription?

No. Codex is only available in the new unified desktop app and on the web at chatgpt.com. Classic is limited to the Chat interface.

Will my chat history disappear if I uninstall ChatGPT Classic?

No. Conversations are stored in your ChatGPT account on OpenAI's servers. Uninstalling either desktop app only removes the local client; history remains accessible in the other app or on the web.
